apps.name: Minecraft
apps.detail: The Minecraft app. Private for now: listed by its local install path, nothing to download.

mods.name: Coordinates
mods.detail: A coordinates corner for the screen: where you stand, the block and chunk you are in, which way you face, the biome and the dimension. Each line can be turned on or off.

mods.name: Create (client support)
mods.detail: What the Jester client needs to join a server that runs Create (the Fabric port "Create Fly", Minecraft 1.21.11). Supplies the mod's blocks, items and menus as modded content.

mods.name: Minecraft Font Test
mods.detail: A plain dark screen that shows Minecraft's own font, read from your copy of the game, so you can judge how it looks.

mods.name: FPS Counter
mods.detail: The frame rate in a corner of the screen, with the frame time and the worst frame of the last few seconds, taken from the engine's own numbers.

mods.name: Host Debug Lines
mods.detail: The machine-level lines of the F3 screen: where the eye is, the window size, the frame rate and which build this is. Published for whatever debug screen is loaded.

mods.name: Survival HUD
mods.detail: A Minecraft-shaped player: a hotbar, hearts, hunger, armour, a level and an inventory screen, with the survival state that gives them meaning.

mods.name: Keystrokes
mods.detail: Your movement keys, the jump bar and the mouse buttons drawn in a corner of the screen, lit while pressed, with clicks per second under each mouse button.

mods.name: Minecraft Ambience
mods.detail: Every sound the Minecraft client chooses to play on its own: cave noises, biome ambience, weather and music, in addition to the sounds a server sends.

mods.name: Debug Screen
mods.detail: The F3 debug screen, where every line is data. Other mods add their own lines instead of editing the game.

mods.name: Join a Minecraft Server
mods.detail: Reads a server address from server.txt and joins it, so a modpack can say which Minecraft server it is for.

mods.name: Minecraft Protocol
mods.detail: The Minecraft network protocol as pure arithmetic: framing, packets and chunks, proved without a server or a socket.

mods.name: Minecraft Plus
mods.detail: The usual client-side quality-of-life mods in one: tooltips for what you look at, a hunger preview, a zoom key, waypoints, a frame-rate limiter and more.

mods.name: Host a Minecraft Server
mods.detail: Single-player as a real Minecraft server running on your own machine, so the world behaves exactly as it does in the real game.

mods.name: Player Skins
mods.detail: Shows other players' skins and capes. Fetches them from textures.minecraft.net over HTTPS, and nothing else is sent anywhere.

mods.name: Minecraft Interface
mods.detail: Minecraft's menus drawn out of your own copy of the game: the main menu with its tiled background, logo and splash, and the in-game screens.

mods.name: Minecraft Import
mods.detail: Imports Minecraft from the copy you already own. Nothing of Mojang's ships with Jester; the textures, sounds, language files and data are read from your game jar.

mods.name: Minimap
mods.detail: A map of the ground around you in a corner of the screen, with waypoints, a death point, an entity radar and the usual info lines.

mods.name: Modded Content Registry
mods.detail: Shared tables for content a Minecraft server mod adds. A library: providers fill it in and the world renderer reads it.

mods.name: Modded Menu Screens
mods.detail: A library for the menus a server mod adds: the layout grammar and the catalogs a provider fills in so a screen can be drawn.

mods.name: Mouse Tweaks
mods.detail: Mouse Tweaks (YaLTeR) for container screens: drag to spread a stack, shift-click to move matching items, scroll to transfer, and the rest of the original.

mods.name: NEI
mods.detail: NotEnoughItems as ChickenBones drew it, beside the inventory screens: the item panel, search, recipes and cheat mode.

mods.name: Sky
mods.detail: The Minecraft sky: the sun, moon and stars, the clouds and the colour of the day, driven by the world clock.

mods.name: Verify: vanilla-derived self-tests
mods.detail: Self-tests that run the real protocol decoders over data a vanilla Minecraft server produced, and report whether they agree.

mods.name: Voxel World
mods.detail: A world made of blocks that you can dig into and build back up. The host side of the voxel engine: drawing, the crosshair and joining a server.

mods.name: WorldEdit (client support)
mods.detail: The client half of WorldEdit: draws your selection (WorldEditCUI) while the server does the editing.
